claims.statement: The `hteam mcp` CLI subcommand invokes `mcp::run`, which opens an authenticated `Session`, constructs `HteamMcpServer` from its client, serves it over rmcp stdio, and waits until the service ends; startup and service errors are written to stderr and propagated.
`HteamMcpServer` owns an `Arc<HteamClient>` and is cloneable, allowing rmcp handlers to share the single authenticated client created for the MCP service lifetime.

The MCP server is a thin delivery adapter over the shared operations layer: operations accept `&HteamClient`, return plain domain data, and explicitly exclude CLI, TUI, and JSON presentation decisions.
`working_stop` accepts a working-on-it record ID rather than a card ID, and the shared operation forwards that identifier to the client stop call.
The MCP server is launched by the `hteam mcp` CLI command, which dispatches `crate::mcp::run()` from the main CLI router.
MCP startup is all-or-nothing: `Session::open()` must succeed before the server begins serving, so invalid or missing credentials prevent an unauthenticated MCP endpoint from starting.
The MCP server uses rmcp's stdio transport and wraps the authenticated `HteamClient` in `Arc` so all tool handlers share one session for the process lifetime.

MCP handlers are thin adapters: `#[tool_router(server_handler)]` registers tool methods, `Parameters<T>` supplies both JSON-RPC deserialization and JSON Schema, and handlers delegate to shared operations instead of reimplementing Hteam request logic.

Successful MCP tool calls are serialized through the `ok` helper as exactly one pretty-printed `Content::text(...)` payload, while operation or serialization failures are converted into MCP internal errors through `err` and `map_err(err)?`.
The stdio MCP path must keep JSON-RPC traffic on stdout/stdin and send diagnostics to stderr; the CLI intentionally skips update notices for `Mcp` so protocol output is not polluted.

The MCP surface includes board, card, comment, working, project, reminder, dashboard, check-in, daily-work, and user-search tools, with card-label mutation tools and follow-up completion/cancellation exposed as separate tool methods.

MCP tool parameters use MCP JSON field names and encode important defaults and invariants in the schema, including optional board scoping, `card_create` requiring `name`, `card_update` requiring `card_id` and `board`, `card_comment` defaulting `follow` to false with optional `date`, and `working_stop` requiring a working-record id rather than a card id.
The MCP tool names are stable integration names that do not mirror the CLI command hierarchy one-to-one, and several tools return domain models rather than terminal-formatted tables.

The MCP adapter must not duplicate business logic: when adding a tool, the recommended extension path is to add or reuse a shared operation that accepts `&HteamClient`, define a schema-backed parameter type, and keep the handler thin.

`hteam mcp` starts `crate::mcp::run()`, which opens one authenticated `Session` and serves `HteamMcpServer` over rmcp stdio; startup fails instead of exposing an unauthenticated endpoint if session credentials are missing or invalid.
The MCP server keeps a single `Arc<HteamClient>` for the whole process lifetime, so all tool handlers share the same authenticated session and client-side state.

MCP tool handlers are thin adapters that deserialize `Parameters<T>` generated from `Deserialize + JsonSchema` parameter structs, invoke shared `operations` functions, and avoid duplicating HTTP or presentation logic.
MCP tool parameter names are JSON field names such as `card_id`, `list_id`, `to_list`, `from_list`, `working_id`, `project_id`, and `activity_type`, not CLI flag names or positional arguments.

Board-scoped MCP reads and moves accept optional `board`, `cards_search` accepts optional `list_id`, and `daily_work` accepts optional `user`, `activity_type`, and `range`; when omitted, those values are resolved by shared session or operation logic rather than reimplemented in the MCP layer.

`card_update` is stricter than most other MCP tools: it requires both `card_id` and `board`, while editable fields remain optional; the handler delegates to the shared full-card update workflow so omitted fields preserve the patch base.
`card_comment` requires `card_id` and `comment`, defaults `follow` to `false`, accepts an optional `date`, and uses the shared comment-date parsing and local-time defaulting from operations.
`working_stop` requires a working-record ID rather than a card ID, so callers must first obtain the record id from `working_list` or a similar working-on-it source.

Successful MCP handlers return exactly one pretty-printed JSON text content item through `CallToolResult::success`, and mutations without a natural domain object respond with explicit JSON acknowledgements such as `{"success": true, ...}`.

Operation failures and serialization failures are both translated into MCP internal errors via `map_err(err)?`, so remote HTTP failures, auth or config problems, and validation errors are surfaced as tool failures instead of success responses containing error text.

The MCP tool surface includes board and card reads, card mutations, comments and follow-ups, working-on-it, project, and people/activity tools; the current server registers 43 tools and keeps tool names stable regardless of the CLI command hierarchy.

MCP defaults differ from some CLI or TUI interactions: `card_move` defaults `from_list` to Open list 1 when omitted, `daily_work` defaults `range` to `today`, and the TUI always supplies its visible source list so it does not accidentally move from Open when the card came from another list.
The MCP server keeps diagnostics on stderr while stdio transport traffic stays on stdout/stdin, which prevents protocol corruption during startup and runtime failures.

When adding new MCP capabilities, the repository expects the domain operation and its `HteamClient` call to be added first, followed by a thin `#[tool]` handler that only maps parameters and chooses the MCP result shape.
